# Goodreads.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/goodreads-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/goodreads-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects book data, ratings and reviews from Goodreads.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Goodreads for Book Data, Ratings, and Reviews](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-goodreads)
- **Code:** [`goodreads.py`](goodreads.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Book pages](results/book.json) · [Review pages](results/reviews.json) · [List pages](results/list.json) · [Search pages](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Goodreads book pages, from their JSON-LD `Book` block and the page markup
- Goodreads book reviews, the review sample a book page ships with, from its `__NEXT_DATA__` Apollo records
- Goodreads list pages, which turn a public list into book stubs and book URLs
- Goodreads book search results, from the `Book` records in the page's Next.js flight data

## Functions

- `scrape_book(url)` → `Dict`: scrape a single book page and return parsed book data
- `scrape_list(url, enrich=False)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape a book list page and return book stubs found on it. if enrich=True, additionally scrape each book's page for full details.
- `scrape_reviews(url)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape the review sample a Goodreads book page ships with
- `scrape_search(query, max_pages=2)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape book stubs from Goodreads search results

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import goodreads


async def main():
    book = await goodreads.scrape_book("https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/4671.The_Great_Gatsby")
    reviews = await goodreads.scrape_reviews("https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/2767052/reviews")
    list = await goodreads.scrape_list(
        "https://www.goodreads.com/list/show/264.Books_That_Everyone_Should_Read",
        enrich=False,
    )
    search = await goodreads.scrape_search("dune", max_pages=2)


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/book.json`](results/book.json): `url`, `title`, `author`, `description`, `image_url`, `genres`, `num_pages`, `format`, `language`, `isbn`, `awards`, `first_published`, `rating`
- [`results/reviews.json`](results/reviews.json): `review_id`, `reviewer`, `reviewer_url`, `rating`, `text`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `likes`, `comments`, `spoiler`
- [`results/list.json`](results/list.json): `rank`, `title`, `url`, `author`, `author_url`, `image_url`, `avg_rating`, `ratings_count`, `score`, `votes`
- [`results/search.json`](results/search.json): `rank`, `title`, `url`, `author`, `author_url`, `image_url`, `avg_rating`, `ratings_count`, `score`, `votes`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`goodreads.py`](goodreads.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/goodreads-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_book_scraping`, `test_review_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`, `test_list_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
